feedback: Several misalignments. (1) `key_found`: once the locked door is unlocked (Door.toggle clears `is_locked`), that's fine here since it uses the view — but the first term should read the previous valuation safely; acceptable. Actually the real problem: `key_found` is fine. (2) `has_matching_key` and `target_door_open` rely on finding the door via `is_locked`, which is cleared after unlocking; the code notes state the locked door's color/cell must be captured before any unlock and kept for the episode. After `has_matching_key` becomes true and the agent toggles the door open, `is_locked` is False, so `target_door_open` scans and finds no locked door — it will return False immediately after unlocking, breaking the latch semantics and the RM (reward would fire at the transition but state reading is unreliable; worse, `has_matching_key` also turns false after unlock since no locked door matches). Both must latch the locked door's identity/color at first evaluation and store it, not rescan `is_locked` each step. (3) `target_door_open` should track the captured locked door's `is_open`. (4) `target_room_entered` has the same flaw: after unlocking, the door scan finds nothing, so entry can never be detected after the door opens. Fix by capturing the locked door's color and cell once (e.g., on first call, when exactly one `is_locked` door exists) and reusing that snapshot. No other issues: no imports, no mutations, syntax is valid, proposition set matches exactly.

feedback: Multiple alignment failures. (1) `has_matching_key`: uses `is_locked` to find the locked door's color, but unlocking clears `is_locked` — after the agent unlocks, the color lookup fails; the fallback branch tries to recover via latching but never learns the color before unlock and wrongly makes `has_matching_key` a latch (it can turn false when the key is dropped). It should capture the locked door's color at first labeling and keep it; simply `env.carrying.color == L`. Also no extra latch semantics are declared for this condition. (2) `target_door_open`: same `is_locked` bug — once the door is unlocked, `is_locked` is False, so the predicate becomes false even if the door stays open; it must find the locked door once (before any unlock) and track its `is_open`, latching color/position for the episode. (3) `target_room_entered`: completely wrong — it only checks whether the agent stands on a currently-locked door cell, never testing the room-block containment as a disjunction with the door cell, and it breaks after unlock (locked doors no longer findable). It must use the remembered locked door cell `(dx,dy)` and test `dx <= ax <= dx+5 and 5*(dy//5) <= ay <= 5*(dy//5)+5` (door cell included in the block, doorway counts as inside) plus the previous-valuation latch. (4) `key_found`: syntactically fine and uses the view reading, but guard `previous_valuation` access — acceptable as written; note `any(cell[0] == 5 ...)` iterating the observation is the intended reading. (5) `target_picked_up`: correct. (6) Boolean fidelity: the `target_room_entered` expression's leading `any(...)` (agent anywhere with any locked door existing) is spurious and can accidentally satisfy the conjunction with an unrelated locked-door cell scan; the semantics is not the declared one. Fix: find the locked door once at episode start (its color and cell), store for reuse, and express each predicate per the code notes.
